title: Exam Blueprint
lead: How the exam itself works: format, timing, scoring, policies, and what it deliberately does not test. For what topics are tested, see Home.

glance.title: Exam details at a glance
glance.source: Source: guide §3 "Exam Details at a Glance".
rows: 60 — multiple-choice and multiple-response; each item states how many responses to select
4 scenarios drawn at random from a bank of 6
Proctored — online proctored and/or test center, per program policy
$125 USD (per attempt — a retake pays again)
12 months from the date the credential is awarded
Pass/fail with scaled score, plus percent-correct by domain

scoring.title: How it's scored
paragraphs: The exam is **criterion-referenced**: you're measured against a fixed performance standard set by a formal standard-setting study, not ranked against other candidates. Passing means demonstrating the blueprint's knowledge and skills at or above that standard — not outperforming a percentage of peers.

Your result is pass/fail with a scaled score (100–1,000, cut score 720). The domain percent-correct breakdown on your score report is diagnostic only — it helps you see where you were weak, but your pass/fail is decided by the total scaled score, not by any single domain's percentage.
scoring.source: Source: guide §10 "How the Exam Is Scored".

policies.title: Policies worth planning around
policies.source: Source: guide §12 "Exam Policies", §13 "Exam-Day Experience and Rules of Conduct", §15 "Credential Maintenance and Recertification".
rows: Valid, unexpired, government-issued photo ID; the name must match your registration exactly
Must be requested and approved by Pearson VUE *before* you schedule — don't book first
14 days after attempt 1, 30 days after attempt 2, 90 days after attempt 3
Up to 4 attempts within a rolling 12-month period; the fee applies every time
Forfeits the exam fee — you must re-register
Stay in webcam view if online; no notes, phones, second monitors, or recording devices; no communicating with anyone; no capturing or reproducing exam content
Can mean an invalidated result, a revoked credential, and a ban from future exams
Free, non-proctored renewal assessment before the 12-month mark; a lapsed credential requires the full exam again at full fee

outOfScope.title: Explicitly out of scope — don't spend study time here
outOfScope.source: Source: guide Appendix, "Out-of-Scope Topics". This list is also enforced in `CLAUDE.md` — no page or quiz question in this workbench is built on any of these.
items: Fine-tuning Claude or training custom models
Claude API authentication, billing, or account management
Language/framework implementation detail beyond tool and schema configuration
Deploying or hosting MCP servers (infrastructure, networking, orchestration)
Claude's internal architecture, training process, or model weights
Constitutional AI, RLHF, or safety-training methodologies
Embedding models or vector-database implementation details
Streaming API implementation or server-sent events
Rate limits, quotas, or API pricing calculations
OAuth, API key rotation, or authentication protocol details
Prompt-caching implementation details (knowing it exists is enough)
